title: Skyscraper complexes preserve acyclicity and recover the stalk complex
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space, let $x\in X$, and let $M^\bullet$ be a cochain complex of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Define the termwise skyscraper complex $i_{x,*}M^\bullet$ by $(i_{x,*}M^n)(U)=M^n$ when $x\in U$ and $0$ otherwise, with $\mathcal O_X(U)$ acting through the germ at $x$. Then $(i_{x,*}M^\bullet)_x\cong M^\bullet$ as complexes of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-modules, and if $M^\bullet$ is acyclic [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules], $i_{x,*}M^\bullet$ is acyclic as a complex of sheaves.

source.place: Sheaves, Definition Tag 009A (label definition-skyscraper-sheaf), case (4), and Lemma Tag 009C (label lemma-stalk-skyscraper-adjoint), applied degreewise; exactness is sectionwise

proof.text: For every degree $i$ and open $U\subseteq X$, the term $(i_{x,*}M^i)(U)$ is $M^i$ when $x\in U$ and the zero module otherwise, and the differential is $d^i_M$ or the zero map accordingly. If $x\in U$, the sequence of sections in degrees $i-1,i,i+1$ is $M^{i-1}\to M^i\to M^{i+1}$, exact by acyclicity of $M^\bullet$; if $x\notin U$, it is the zero sequence, which is exact. Thus $i_{x,*}M^{i-1}\to i_{x,*}M^i\to i_{x,*}M^{i+1}$ is sectionwise exact, hence exact as a sequence of sheaves, for every $i$. By the definition of acyclicity, $i_{x,*}M^\bullet$ is acyclic.

source.place: Definition Tag 009A (label definition-skyscraper-sheaf), case (4), and Lemma Tag 009C (label lemma-stalk-skyscraper-adjoint), applied degreewise; exactness is sectionwise

proof.text: The stalk at $x$ of each term $i_{x,*}M^i$ is the filtered colimit over open neighbourhoods $U$ of $x$ of $(i_{x,*}M^i)(U)$. Every such value is $M^i$ and every transition map is the identity, so this colimit is canonically $M^i$. These identifications commute with the differentials, since all restriction maps and differentials are defined termwise from those of $M^\bullet$. They therefore assemble to an isomorphism of cochain complexes $(i_{x,*}M^\bullet)_x\cong M^\bullet$, and since $\mathcal O_X(U)$ acts through the germ at $x$, the $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-module structures agree.
